text:
It is truly heartwarming to observe how cinema has so generously simplified the human experience, replacing the gnawing anxiety of adolescence with the rhythmic certainty of a well-timed hip thrust. We are taught that the crushing weight of social hierarchy and existential dread can be neatly resolved by breaking into song, because nothing says "emotional maturity" like harmonizing with your enemies while wearing a varsity jacket.

In this brave new world, the primary material of a candle is not wax, but rather the collective delusion that we are all secretly talented Broadway performers waiting for the right lighting cue. We burn through our youth not in tears or confusion, but in a blaze of choreographed perfection, convinced that if we just jump high enough and hit the high note, the principal will finally understand our feelings about homework. It is a beautiful, terrifying lie: that life is not a series of awkward silences and failed tests, but a continuous, seamless musical number where everyone knows the lyrics and nobody ever misses a step.
